subject.title: fix(sqlite): allow verified shared wal backports

question: Should OpenClaw support shared-system SQLite distro backports through a permanent operator-controlled bypass, and if so what verifiable package/build contract is sufficient to prevent bypassing the WAL-corruption guard on an unpatched library?
rationale: The code can be made mechanically correct, but only maintainers can decide whether an operator assertion is an acceptable safety policy and what durable support boundary OpenClaw should guarantee.

options.title: Retain fail-closed behavior
options.body: Reject unrecognized shared SQLite builds and direct operators to a Node/runtime distribution whose SQLite safety status OpenClaw can support.

options.title: Define a build-bound exception
options.body: Specify a supported distro/package identity, verification method, documentation, and tests before accepting a narrowly scoped backport path.

options.title: Accept an operator assertion
options.body: Allow the environment override as a documented unsupported-at-own-risk escape hatch and explicitly own the resulting support and corruption-risk tradeoff.

recommendation.title: Retain fail-closed behavior
recommendation.body: Reject unrecognized shared SQLite builds and direct operators to a Node/runtime distribution whose SQLite safety status OpenClaw can support.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently contributed the merged adjacent work that documents the same WAL-safety boundary, though ownership evidence is limited.
